description: Fig. 12 is a four-panel composite of micro-DIC statistical line plots, panels (a)-(d), all sharing identical axes: Average Shear Strain (%) on the y-axis (labelled 2-18, gridlines every 2) versus Engineering Strain (%) on the x-axis (labelled 4-20, ticks every 2). No numeric values are printed on the curves; every point carries an error bar. (a) RD sample compares γ+α (RD) (red open triangles, dashed) with δ (RD) (red filled squares, solid): the two curves nearly coincide, rising from just under 4% shear strain near 5% engineering strain to about the 15 gridline at 20%. (b) TD sample compares γ+α (TD) (purple open circles, solid) with δ (TD) (purple filled triangles, dashed): δ lies clearly above γ+α at every strain, ending near 15% versus about 12% at 20%. (c) RD, γ-α' (RD) (green dashed) versus α (RD) (blue dashed): γ-α' is systematically higher, reaching roughly 16.5% versus about 13% at 20%. (d) TD, γ-α' (TD) versus α (TD): same ordering, γ-α' about 15% versus α about 11.5% at 20%. The panels jointly demonstrate strain partitioning: negligible between δ-ferrite and γ+α aggregates in RD but pronounced in TD, and always toward the austenite-bearing γ-α' mixed phase in both.
measured_quantities: strain partitioning ratio between phases (dimensionless, e.g. δ/γ+α and γ-α'/α)

observations.observation: All four panels share the same axes: x = Engineering Strain (%) labelled from 4 to 20 with ticks every 2; y = Average Shear Strain (%) labelled from 2 to 18 with ticks every 2.

In panel (a) the γ+α (RD) and δ (RD) curves lie almost exactly on top of one another over the whole strain range, with their error bars overlapping, indicating negligible average-strain partitioning between δ-ferrite and the UFG γ+α aggregates in the RD sample.

In panel (b) the δ (TD) curve (purple filled triangles, dashed) lies above the γ+α (TD) curve (purple open circles, solid) at every plotted strain, and the gap between them exceeds the drawn error bars and widens with strain.

In panels (c) and (d) the γ-α' curve (green dashed) lies above the α curve (blue dashed) at all strains, showing more shear strain concentrated in the γ-α' mixed phase than in α for both RD and TD samples.
At the largest plotted engineering strain (the point on the 20% tick) the δ (TD) data point in (b) sits just below the 15% shear-strain gridline while the γ+α (TD) point sits on the 12% gridline.

At the 20% engineering-strain tick in (c) the γ-α' (RD) point lies just above the 16% gridline and the α (RD) point between the 12% and 14% gridlines; in (d) the corresponding points lie near the 15% and just above the 11-12% level respectively.
Every data point in all four panels carries a vertical error bar, and the error bars are visibly larger at the highest strains (15% and 20% engineering strain) than at 5%.
The caption states that panels (a) and (b) give the average shear strain of δ-ferrite and UFG γ+α regions in (a) RD and (b) TD as a function of engineering strain.
The caption states that panels (c) and (d) give the average shear strain of the γ-α' mixed phase and the α phase within UFG γ+α regions in (c) RD and (d) TD as a function of engineering strain.

The citing text states that in the RD sample the average strain values remain quite similar between δ-ferrite and the UFG γ+α aggregates, whereas in the TD sample the average strain of δ-ferrite is about 1.26 times higher than that of the γ+α aggregates.
The citing text states that for both samples more strain is concentrated in the γ-α' mixed phase, up to 1.3 times higher than in the α phase.

The citing text states that the strain partitioning between α and γ-α' is already notable at small strains (5%), where martensite formation is relatively limited, indicating a mechanical contrast origin.

The citing text states that the plastic strain concentrated in the austenite phase is higher in the RD sample than in the TD sample by a factor of ~1.15, based on comparing panels (c) and (d) (ε_RD = 1.15 ε_TD).

The citing text attributes the lower austenite strain of the TD sample to the higher strain concentration within the δ-ferrite phase, given that the α versus γ-α' partitioning ratio is similar between the two samples.

subfigures.description: Line plot of Average Shear Strain (%) vs Engineering Strain (%) for the RD sample, with two nearly superimposed curves: γ+α (RD) (red open triangles, dashed) and δ (RD) (red filled squares, solid). Both rise from just under 4% at ~5% engineering strain to about 15% at 20%; error bars overlap along the whole curve.

Same axes for the TD sample: δ (TD) (purple filled triangles, dashed) lies above γ+α (TD) (purple open circles, solid) at every plotted strain, the separation exceeding the error bars; δ approaches the 15 gridline and γ+α about the 12 gridline at 20% engineering strain.

Same axes for the RD sample comparing phases inside the UFG region: γ-α' (RD) (green dashed) is above α (RD) (blue dashed) at all strains, reaching roughly 16.5% versus about 13% average shear strain at 20% engineering strain, with error bars growing at higher strain.
Same axes for the TD sample: γ-α' (TD) (green dashed) remains above α (TD) (blue dashed) at all strains, reaching about 15% versus about 11.5% average shear strain at 20% engineering strain.
